rows.name: AvGetSavedDataAddress
rows.rationale: One pointer load; already minimal.
rows.risk: Preserve ABI, existing errors, ordering and ownership.

rows.name: AvSendTVEncoderOption
rows.rationale: GET_SETTINGS makes two live reads; VIDEO_ENABLE probes up to two encoders then gates/DAC writes. Live state and hardware failures rule out unchecked caching. Unsupported filters/options are currently no-ops.
rows.risk: Preserve device reads/writes; encoder/filter support remains incomplete.

rows.name: AvSetDisplayMode
rows.rationale: One CRTC_START write, four index/data pairs, two data reads preserve unrelated pitch bits. Required device traffic; cannot suppress repeated writes based on guessed device state.
rows.risk: Existing mode/format/step handling is incomplete and framebuffer mask is 64 MiB; this audit does not repair video behavior.

rows.name: AvSetSavedDataAddress
rows.rationale: One pointer store; address is mutable, no cache needed.
rows.risk: Preserve ABI, existing errors, ordering and ownership.

rows.name: DbgBreakPoint
rows.rationale: int3/ret leaf; exception cost is requested behavior.
rows.risk: Retain title SEH and debugger delivery.

rows.name: DbgBreakPointWithStatus
rows.rationale: Argument load, breakpoint and stack-cleaning return; already minimal.
rows.risk: Preserve EAX status and calling convention.

rows.name: DbgLoadImageSymbols
rows.rationale: Unmapped ordinal generates a correct-arity fatal stub; similarly named RTL function is not the export target. No successful implementation to optimize.

rows.name: DbgPrint
rows.rationale: Release DBG=0 returns STATUS_SUCCESS without formatting or transport. Matched checked DBG=1 formats into bounded512-byte stack buffer with reentrancy/SEH handling, then calls DebugPrint/KdpPrint for log/debugger transport. Stub verdict applies to release only.
rows.risk: Checked transport/formatting differs; do not remove its output under release assumption.

rows.name: HalReadSMCTrayState
rows.rationale: One live register read, constant-size state normalization and optional count. Bus polling dominates; caching hides tray changes/errors.
rows.risk: SMC ISR is absent; eject counter stays zero. Preserve open fallback/error status.

rows.rationale: Both matched variants return0 after optional Response[0]=NUL: release directly; checked DBG=1 calls NxkDebuggerPromptAvailable, whose !KDBG branch returns FALSE because checked defines do not enable KDBG. The later bounded prompt scan/DebugPrompt transport is unreachable in these builds.
rows.risk: Preserve initial NUL/count; attached debugger input is unverified.

rows.name: DbgUnLoadImageSymbols
rows.rationale: Unmapped ordinal generates a correct-arity fatal stub; similarly named RTL function is not the export target. No successful implementation to optimize.

rows.name: ExAcquireReadWriteLockExclusive
rows.backend: ExAcquireReadWriteLockExclusive -> Xbox ERWLOCK / KeWaitForSingleObject, KeSetEvent, KeReleaseSemaphore
rows.rationale: One interrupt-mask window and atomic contention increment; uncontended acquire returns, contended writers wait on the auto-reset event. Eliminating masking or bypassing writer ownership would alter exclusion.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: ExAcquireReadWriteLockShared
rows.backend: ExAcquireReadWriteLockShared -> Xbox ERWLOCK / KeWaitForSingleObject, KeSetEvent, KeReleaseSemaphore
rows.rationale: One masked increment with reader/writer queue checks; readers share the lock only when no writer is ahead. Existing common path is constant work; the semaphore wait is required contention handling.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: ExAllocatePool
rows.rationale: Implicit NonPagedPool adapter; small allocations use a constant-time size-class lookup and one free-list pop under NxpLock. Class refills and >2040-byte requests reach the repeated pool-window range search; failure reclaim retries once.
rows.risk: Low to medium: scan boundary mistakes can change returned VA or false-fail allocation; fast empty-window cases may see no benefit.
rows.measurement: Run the actual baseline and candidate kernel implementation through the exported ordinal in the same release compiler/xemu 128-MiB configuration and immutable guest ISO; at least seven paired trials, alternating order; retain all samples, median and variation. Check exact outputs/state and operation counters first; claim timing improvement only beyond observed variation. No measurements were executed in this read-only audit. Allocate actual pool runs of 1/2/4/16/256/1024 pages; construct dense, alternating, free-prefix-before-blocker and full-window patterns; compare chosen VA/failure and freed-page accounting. Count tested bits/bitmap loads, candidate probes, PFN operations and lock duration. A 4096-page map with occupied every 256th page and Count=256 gives an illustrative source-model 493696 bit checks versus 4096 with conflict skipping; this is a counted algorithm model, not a measured kernel speedup.

rows.name: ExAllocatePoolWithTag
rows.rationale: Adds no material work beyond the required tag and NonPagedPool arguments. Active nxpool handles an 8-byte header and size-class pop; fresh pages/big blocks use pool-window scan and per-page mapping, with bounded 128-entry big-block tracking.
rows.risk: Low to medium: scan boundary mistakes can change returned VA or false-fail allocation; fast empty-window cases may see no benefit.

rows.name: ExEventObjectType
rows.backend: XeExEventObjectType -> Xbox public object-type data / native type mapping
rows.rationale: 28-byte Xbox OBJECT_TYPE storage with NULL procedure pointers and type PoolTag, mapped to native type internally; data-only ABI, no callable work.
rows.risk: Preserve ordinal address, size/layout, storage lifetime and mutable publication; no optimization proposed.

rows.name: ExFreePool
rows.rationale: One tagless adapter. Small free validates magic then pushes one class-list entry and decrements live count; page-aligned free scans at most 128 tracking slots and returns/unmaps each page with a TLB invalidation. Those lifetime operations are required; no measured evidence favors new tracking complexity. Checked pool frees also record last-freer attribution, unlike release.
rows.risk: Preserve mapping, pins, persistence, page supply, IRQL/lock order, failure unwind and TLB visibility.

rows.name: ExInitializeReadWriteLock
rows.backend: ExInitializeReadWriteLock -> Xbox ERWLOCK; event/semaphore dispatcher waits
rows.rationale: Four counter stores and event/semaphore initialization. These establish the public ERWLOCK state; no allocation or scan to remove.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: ExInterlockedAddLargeInteger
rows.rationale: Interrupt exclusion and caller spinlock protect the 64-bit read/add/write, returning the old value. UP spinlock helpers already collapse; preserve interrupt state and the three-argument contract.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: ExInterlockedAddLargeStatistic
rows.rationale: Active i386 assembly uses add/adc on UP, with no generic-C stub reached. Two arithmetic instructions and return; carry propagation and current atomicity contract cannot be shortened safely.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: ExInterlockedCompareExchange64
rows.rationale: Three pointer arguments are dereferenced into the intrinsic 64-bit compare/exchange. Already one atomic operation; no reusable-work candidate.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: ExMutantObjectType
rows.backend: XeExMutantObjectType -> Xbox public object-type data / native type mapping
rows.rationale: 28-byte Xbox OBJECT_TYPE storage with NULL procedure pointers and type PoolTag, mapped to native type internally; data-only ABI, no callable work.
rows.risk: Preserve ordinal address, size/layout, storage lifetime and mutable publication; no optimization proposed.

rows.name: ExQueryPoolBlockSize
rows.rationale: A one-argument adapter supplying a local quota flag. Small-block size is an O(1) header/class lookup; big blocks inspect at most 128 tracked records under lock. Tracking saturation already returns zero for untracked big allocations; do not conceal that limitation with a guessed size.
rows.risk: Preserve mapping, pins, persistence, page supply, IRQL/lock order, failure unwind and TLB visibility.

rows.name: ExQueryNonVolatileSetting
rows.rationale: First successful load reads 256 bytes once; warm query scans 24 settings plus at most four section descriptors. Ordinary output zeroing scales with caller length and is required; image/open cache already avoids repeated bus/decryption work.
rows.risk: Preserve sealed-tail and short-buffer out-parameter rules; failed load/open retries and mutable cached image.

rows.name: ExReadWriteRefurbInfo
rows.rationale: Allocates 512-byte sector; opens/reads/closes Partition0, writes reopen/write/close. Read-before-write preserves other 496 bytes. Handle/record caching requires lifetime/error contracts; infrequent persistence path merits no change.
rows.risk: Preserve exact record size, marker and complete sector bytes/errors.

rows.name: ExRaiseException
rows.backend: RtlRaiseException -> i386 RTL SEH capture / RtlDispatchException
rows.rationale: Alias to active i386 RtlRaiseException assembly captures registers/context and dispatches SEH; handlers may continue execution. Frame walking and context preservation are required, not redundant wrapper work.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: ExRaiseStatus
rows.backend: RtlRaiseStatus -> i386 RTL SEH capture / RtlDispatchException
rows.rationale: Alias to active i386 RtlRaiseStatus builds a noncontinuable record, captures context, dispatches and raises. Error behavior and register preservation preclude a success shortcut.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: ExReleaseReadWriteLock
rows.backend: ExReleaseReadWriteLock -> Xbox ERWLOCK / KeWaitForSingleObject, KeSetEvent, KeReleaseSemaphore
rows.rationale: Masked decrement returns immediately when free; otherwise hands ownership to a batch of readers or the next writer. Required wake count and fairness transitions account for the work.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: ExSaveNonVolatileSetting
rows.rationale: Fixed descriptor scan, zero/copy setting, 23-word checksum and four checksum bytes plus setting-byte writes. Skipping unchanged writes changes errors/device transactions; whole-section checksum overlap must retain behavior.
rows.risk: Preserve writable indices, partial writes, checksum-before-setting ordering and cache mutation.

rows.name: ExSemaphoreObjectType
rows.backend: XeExSemaphoreObjectType -> Xbox public object-type data / native type mapping
rows.rationale: 28-byte Xbox OBJECT_TYPE storage with NULL procedure pointers and type PoolTag, mapped to native type internally; data-only ABI, no callable work.
rows.risk: Preserve ordinal address, size/layout, storage lifetime and mutable publication; no optimization proposed.

rows.name: ExTimerObjectType
rows.backend: XeExTimerObjectType -> Xbox public object-type data / native type mapping
rows.rationale: 28-byte Xbox OBJECT_TYPE storage with NULL procedure pointers and type PoolTag, mapped to native type internally; data-only ABI, no callable work.
rows.risk: Preserve ordinal address, size/layout, storage lifetime and mutable publication; no optimization proposed.

rows.name: ExfInterlockedInsertHeadList
rows.backend: XbExfInterlockedInsertHeadList -> Xbox interrupt-masked intrusive list splice
rows.rationale: Masks interrupts, performs one head splice and restores the original enable state; returns the displaced neighbor or NULL. Already constant work with the Xbox two-argument ABI.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: ExfInterlockedInsertTailList
rows.backend: XbExfInterlockedInsertTailList -> Xbox interrupt-masked intrusive list splice
rows.rationale: Masks interrupts, performs one tail splice and restores the original enable state; returns the displaced neighbor or NULL. No redundant allocation or traversal.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: ExfInterlockedRemoveHeadList
rows.backend: XbExfInterlockedRemoveHeadList -> Xbox interrupt-masked intrusive list splice
rows.rationale: Masks interrupts and checks empty before one head unlink, restoring flags. Returning NULL for empty and atomic list linkage are necessary.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: FscGetCacheSize
rows.rationale: One active-block counter read times four pages; no traversal or allocation. Actual block size is 16 KiB, unlike the stale assigned map comment suggesting 64-KiB blocks.
rows.risk: Preserve mapping, pins, persistence, page supply, IRQL/lock order, failure unwind and TLB visibility.

rows.name: FscInvalidateIdleBlocks
rows.rationale: One mutex acquisition and bounded 34-slot pass; only clean, idle, nonbusy mapped blocks lose LRU/map validity, and buffers remain allocated. Skipping dirty/pinned/busy blocks is required; an extra index adds mutable metadata to an already tiny scan.
rows.risk: Preserve mapping, pins, persistence, page supply, IRQL/lock order, failure unwind and TLB visibility.

rows.name: FscSetCacheSize
rows.rationale: Rounds pages to 16-KiB blocks and clamps 4..32 active blocks; grows by required buffer allocations and shrinks only idle nonbusy blocks, flushing dirty valid data. Shrink restarts after flush unlocks because the table can change; replacing this restart with a stale cursor risks pins/ownership. Pool scan candidate benefits growth indirectly.
rows.risk: Preserve mapping, pins, persistence, page supply, IRQL/lock order, failure unwind and TLB visibility.

rows.name: HalClearSoftwareInterrupt
rows.rationale: Single pending-bit clear; minimal.
rows.risk: Preserve pending-bit ownership.

rows.name: HalDisableSystemInterrupt
rows.rationale: IRQ-range adapter; IDR update and two PIC reads/two writes under interrupt exclusion. Hardware mask read/modify/write cannot become unchecked cached value.
rows.risk: Preserve software IDR, native IRQ ownership and volatile I/O.

rows.name: HalDiskCachePartitionCount
rows.rationale: Generated zero ULONG_PTR XbExpData_40 scaffold (4 bytes). Direct storage access, no per-export call/scan/allocation.
rows.risk: Preserve size/alignment/layout/address/content and mutable consumers.

rows.name: HalDiskModelNumber
rows.rationale: 8-byte model ANSI_STRING and referenced buffer. Direct storage access, no per-export call/scan/allocation.
rows.risk: Preserve size/alignment/layout/address/content and mutable consumers.

rows.name: HalDiskSerialNumber
rows.rationale: 8-byte serial ANSI_STRING and referenced buffer. Direct storage access, no per-export call/scan/allocation.
rows.risk: Preserve size/alignment/layout/address/content and mutable consumers.

rows.name: HalEnableSystemInterrupt
rows.rationale: IRQ-range adapter; optional level-dismiss update, IDR change and two mask writes. Native retry dispatch intentionally stays for edge-forced IRQs.
rows.risk: Preserve mode/native ISR retry and mask/IRQL relationship.

rows.name: HalGetInterruptVector
rows.rationale: Adapter fills fixed ISA/bus arguments; backend references handler, initializes outputs, validates IRQ and computes vector/IRQL. Direct formula bypasses bus absence/output/error behavior.
rows.risk: Preserve unsupported IRQ/default outputs and handler references.

rows.name: HalReadSMBusValue
rows.rationale: Read checks output, shifts address and selects width; writes result only on success. Shared backend bounds idle to 65536 polls and each of 50 attempts to 131072 completion polls plus retry stall. Required device access/retry behavior is not optimizable by skipping reads.
rows.risk: Preserve port widths/order, status bits, bounded polls/retries/stalls and live errors.

rows.name: HalReadWritePCISpace
rows.rationale: Read/write adapter shares lock across validated slot and arbitrary-offset byte/word/dword cycles. Existing width selection handles alignment/tails; larger access batching cannot skip mandatory hardware cycles.
rows.risk: Preserve config lock, slot blacklist, offsets/lengths and volatile ordering.

rows.name: HalRegisterShutdownNotification
rows.rationale: Unregister scans registered/pending; new registration separately scans duplicate and priority under spin lock. One full scan can remember insertion while still checking all duplicates.
rows.risk: Medium: lifecycle-sensitive and low frequency; time benefit may be immaterial.

measurement.structural_bound: Unique registration visits n nodes for duplicate plus p<=n for insertion under spin lock; avoid second p visits.
measurement.recipe: Actual n0,1,8,64,512 high/low/middle/equal priorities and duplicate storage with changed priority; count n+p ->n and lock-held cycles. Capture callback order; unregister unknown/pending/in callback, late registration, nested power SEH/parking; no duplicate callback/use-after-free. Include negative priorities/LONG_MIN/LONG_MAX and duplicate registrations at every original list position.
measurement.timing_protocol: Proposed, not run. Actual changed implementation, identical compiler/defines, guest ISO/inputs and xemu128-MiB; at least seven paired alternating-order baseline/candidate trials. Retain every sample; report median and variation. Claim time gain only above variation, otherwise verified work counts. No Docker/build/binary execution in audit.

rows.name: HalRequestSoftwareInterrupt
rows.rationale: Save IF, disable, set pending bit, invoke eligible software IRQ, restore IF. Exclusion/immediate delivery are required.
rows.risk: Preserve APC/DPC/IRQL/IF semantics.

rows.name: HalReturnToFirmware
rows.rationale: PASSIVE/IF-on path may walk six diagnostic frames, persist launch intent, flush FSDs, drain callbacks and publish handoff. Emergency path bypasses locks. Required durability/lifecycle work outweighs tiny adapter cost.
rows.risk: Preserve noreturn, nested-owner SEH/parking, critical region/special APCs and warm-reset handoff.

rows.name: HalWriteSMBusValue
rows.rationale: Write shifts address/truncates data to selected width. Shared backend bounds idle to 65536 polls and each of 50 attempts to 131072 completion polls plus retry stall. Required device access/retry behavior is not optimizable by skipping reads.
rows.risk: Preserve port widths/order, status bits, bounded polls/retries/stalls and live errors.

rows.name: InterlockedCompareExchange
rows.rationale: Fastcall adapter delegates to one compiler atomic compare/exchange intrinsic and returns the previous value; no scan, allocation or avoidable backend work.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: InterlockedDecrement
rows.rationale: Fastcall adapter performs one atomic decrement and returns the new value. Removing the atomic operation would weaken synchronization.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: InterlockedIncrement
rows.rationale: Fastcall adapter performs one atomic increment and returns the new value; already the primitive required by the ABI.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: InterlockedExchange
rows.rationale: Fastcall adapter performs one atomic exchange and returns the old value. No concrete source-level redundant cost.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: InterlockedExchangeAdd
rows.rationale: Fastcall adapter performs one atomic exchange-add and returns the old value; synchronization and wrap behavior must remain.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: InterlockedFlushSList
rows.rationale: Active i386 assembly flush uses a CMPXCHG8B retry loop to clear link/depth while preserving sequence handling. Retry is required under interference; do not substitute the incompatible generic adapter.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: InterlockedPopEntrySList
rows.rationale: Xbox adapter packs link/depth/sequence into a CMPXCHG8B loop; empty returns immediately. The ordinal-map comment about RTL forwarding is stale: source is inline CAS. ABA sequence and entry lifetime prohibit an unchecked pointer-only pop.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: InterlockedPushEntrySList
rows.rationale: Xbox adapter writes Entry->Next and updates the packed header in a CAS loop. Depth and existing push sequence behavior must remain; no broad optimization without contention evidence.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: IoAllocateIrp
rows.rationale: FALSE-quota adapter. P/L small/large IRP lookasides already precede pool. Stack sizes 2-8 deliberately reuse eight-stack packets and zero advertised PacketSize; skipping dirty unused bytes changes initialization.
rows.risk: Preserve flags/lookaside pairing, stack layout, pool lifetime and zeroing.

rows.name: IoBuildAsynchronousFsdRequest
rows.rationale: One IRP plus buffered Length-byte allocation/write-copy, direct MDL/probe/pins, or pointer-only neither I/O. Flush/shutdown/PNP/power already skip buffer setup. Required asynchronous ownership rules preclude generic direct-buffer shortcut.
rows.risk: Preserve major function, probe direction, pins/failure cleanup and IOSB/thread lifetime.

rows.name: IoBuildDeviceIoControlRequest
rows.rationale: IRP plus METHOD_BUFFERED max input/output buffer and copy; direct method input copy/output pins; METHOD_NEITHER pointers. Thread queueing provides cleanup. No redundant generic buffer operation shown.
rows.risk: Preserve method, sizes, probe direction, thread cancellation and all failure cleanup.

rows.name: IoBuildSynchronousFsdRequest
rows.rationale: Already shares setup then sets event and queues to requestor cancellation list. Event/queue are necessary ownership, not duplicate work.
rows.risk: Preserve event/IOSB and thread-exit cleanup.

rows.name: IoCheckShareAccess
rows.rationale: Constant-size access/share bit tests, six compatibility checks and optional counters. FileObject flags are set even before sharing failure. No allocations/scans; minimal.
rows.risk: Preserve extension skip, paired ownership and Update/zero-access semantics.

rows.name: IoCompletionObjectType
rows.rationale: 28-byte XeIoCompletionObjectType struct, not native POBJECT_TYPE. Direct storage access, no per-export call/scan/allocation.
rows.risk: Preserve size/alignment/layout/address/content and mutable consumers.

rows.name: IoCreateDevice
rows.rationale: Optional one Unicode allocation then native device/extension/VPB/queue and object/driver links. Title provenance matters. Conversion failure currently falls through to unnamed creation; shortcuts need failure equivalence.
rows.risk: Preserve title-owned DRIVER_OBJECT bounds, device extension and conversion failure behavior.

rows.name: IoCreateFile
rows.backend: XeIoCreateFile -> XeTranslateOa -> native file service -> IopCreateFile
rows.rationale: Counted ANSI conversion; drive/pseudo-root prefix builds an ANSI allocation/copy then Unicode allocation, then namespace/share/FSD work. Fusion appears attractive but USHORT overflow and first-allocation fallback alter errors/root interpretation; no unchecked one-allocation path recommended.
rows.risk: Preserve -3/-4 pseudo handles, roots/counts, create Options distinction, cleanup and exact failure branches.

rows.name: IoCreateSymbolicLink
rows.backend: XeIoCreateSymbolicLink -> two conversions -> native link object
rows.rationale: Two Unicode temporaries before object captures name/target; second conversion failure frees first. Namespace caching changes collision/target visibility; infrequent object setup merits no change.
rows.risk: Preserve ABI, existing errors, ordering and ownership.

rows.name: IoDeleteDevice
rows.rationale: Stops/frees optional timer, publishes internal/title DeletePending and unloads after ReferenceCount zero. Required deferred ownership work.
rows.risk: Preserve cancellation/DeletePending and outstanding device lifetime.

rows.name: IoDeleteSymbolicLink
rows.rationale: One conversion allocation plus mandatory namespace lookup/lifetime; wrapper is small.
rows.risk: Preserve ABI, existing errors, ordering and ownership.

rows.name: IoDeviceObjectType
rows.rationale: 28-byte XeIoDeviceObjectType struct. Direct storage access, no per-export call/scan/allocation.
rows.risk: Preserve size/alignment/layout/address/content and mutable consumers.

rows.name: IoFileObjectType
rows.rationale: 28-byte XeIoFileObjectType struct. Direct storage access, no per-export call/scan/allocation.
rows.risk: Preserve size/alignment/layout/address/content and mutable consumers.

rows.name: IoFreeIrp
rows.rationale: Uses allocation flags, depth checks, quota float/accounting; already reuses fixed-size packets. Generic direct pool free breaks pairing.
rows.risk: Preserve packet allocator pairing and thread/completion ownership.

rows.name: IoInitializeIrp
rows.rationale: Zeroes all PacketSize bytes then installs header/stack/APC environment/thread list. Skipping unused bytes changes caller-visible initialization.
rows.risk: Preserve ABI, existing errors, ordering and ownership.

rows.name: IoInvalidDeviceRequest
rows.rationale: Only returns STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_REQUEST; intentionally does not complete or mutate IRP. Minimal.
rows.risk: Do not complete caller-owned IRP as optimization.

rows.name: IoQueryFileInformation
rows.rationale: Only three classes accepted; class fixes length regardless of caller Length. Shared query references/locks file, allocates IRP, supplies caller system buffer, dispatches and waits pending. Local object-field shortcut bypasses title FSDs.
rows.risk: Preserve class/length policy, nonoptional ReturnedLength and pending/file-lock lifetime.

rows.name: IoQueryVolumeInformation
rows.rationale: Four volume classes accepted; caller Length passes unchanged. Shared query references/locks file, allocates IRP, supplies caller system buffer, dispatches and waits pending. Local object-field shortcut bypasses title FSDs.
rows.risk: Preserve class/length policy, nonoptional ReturnedLength and pending/file-lock lifetime.

rows.name: IoQueueThreadIrp
rows.rationale: One wrapper around insertion into Thread->IrpList while a guarded region disables special kernel APCs against completion. No allocation/scan or IRQL raise in inline backend; queueing is required ownership.
rows.risk: Preserve special-APC exclusion and thread cancellation/exit cleanup.

rows.name: IoRemoveShareAccess
rows.rationale: Constant-size access checks and seven counter subtractions. No allocations/scans; minimal.
rows.risk: Preserve extension skip, paired ownership and Update/zero-access semantics.

rows.name: IoSetIoCompletion
rows.rationale: FALSE-quota adapter; P/L lookaside before pool, fills one independent packet then enqueues. Reusing one outstanding packet is invalid.
rows.risk: Preserve wakeups, packet lifetime and resource failure.

rows.name: IoSetShareAccess
rows.rationale: Constant-size access flags and initial counters/zero stores. No allocations/scans; minimal.
rows.risk: Preserve extension skip, paired ownership and Update/zero-access semantics.

rows.name: IoStartNextPacket
rows.rationale: FALSE-cancelable FIFO/deferred native start. Adapter adds no allocation/copy.
rows.risk: Preserve key/FIFO/deferred ordering, CurrentIrp and mutable StartIo callback.

rows.name: IoStartNextPacketByKey
rows.rationale: FALSE-cancelable keyed/deferred native start. Adapter adds no allocation/copy.
rows.risk: Preserve key/FIFO/deferred ordering, CurrentIrp and mutable StartIo callback.

rows.name: IoStartPacket
rows.rationale: NULL cancellation routine; native raises IRQL/queues/starts first packet. Adapter adds no allocation/copy.
rows.risk: Preserve key/FIFO/deferred ordering, CurrentIrp and mutable StartIo callback.

rows.name: IoSynchronousDeviceIoControlRequest
rows.rationale: Stack event/IOSB plus builder, one driver call and wait only for pending. IOCTL also copies Information to returned length. Already small; removing wait/event loses pending completion lifetime.
rows.risk: Preserve builder failures, dispatch/completion status and stack event/IOSB ownership.

rows.name: IoSynchronousFsdRequest
rows.rationale: Stack event/IOSB plus builder, one driver call and wait only for pending. IOCTL also copies Information to returned length. Already small; removing wait/event loses pending completion lifetime.
rows.risk: Preserve builder failures, dispatch/completion status and stack event/IOSB ownership.

rows.name: IofCallDriver
rows.rationale: Decrements/validates stack, stores target device then indirect dispatch. Mandatory mutable table; bypass loses title hooks.
rows.risk: Preserve stack exhaustion bugcheck and stack/callback visibility.

rows.name: IofCompleteRequest
rows.rationale: Walks consumed stack for error/pending/callback state, respects MORE_PROCESSING_REQUIRED; handles associated/paging IRPs, MDL unlocks, and deferred/APC completion. Work manages independent lifetime; no safe generic bypass.
rows.risk: Preserve cancellation, SG callback cleanup, pins, pending and callbacks retaining IRP.

rows.name: KdDebuggerEnabled
rows.rationale: DBG=0 release storage is FALSE; debugger protocol is unlinked by ntos.cmake and this variable has no callable cost. Checked DBG=1 instead links mutable KD64 globals at ntoskrnl/kd64/kddata.c:82.

rows.rationale: Required delay loop handles pending APCs, relative/absolute deadline recalculation, timer insertion and context switch; stack-swap setup is already disabled for Xbox. No safe unmeasured wait shortcut.

rows.name: KeInsertDeviceQueue
rows.backend: KeInsertDeviceQueue -> Native intrusive device queue + Xbox IRQL-only exclusion

rows.name: KeInsertQueue

rows.name: KeInsertQueueApc

rows.measurement: 10000 serial same-thread APC deliveries, callback requeue chain, blocked target bursts 1/8/64/256, duplicate inserts, failed insertion and target termination with/without title rundown. Count pool transactions, peak retained blocks, lookaside hits/misses and title callback/delete counts; capped warm serial traffic should avoid repeated pool calls, cold/burst fallback must match ownership. Include allocation OOM and teardown/relaunch. After implementation, execute actual baseline/candidate export paths with identical compiler, xemu configuration, immutable inputs and guest ISO; alternate order for at least seven paired trials, retain all samples and report median/variation. Claim timing improvement only beyond observed variation; otherwise report verified work reduction.

rows.name: KePulseEvent

rows.name: KeRemoveDeviceQueue
rows.backend: KeRemoveDeviceQueue -> Native intrusive device queue + Xbox IRQL-only exclusion
rows.rationale: One locked head removal or busy-clear when empty. Constant work with required Inserted update.

rows.backend: KeResetEvent -> Dispatcher event/mutant/semaphore wait and wake
rows.rationale: Dispatcher exclusion captures previous state and clears state; constant leaf work plus potentially necessary dispatcher exit.

rows.rationale: Computes saturation/clamp/base-relative priority and quantum under dispatcher/thread coordination, only moving ready state when priority differs. Arithmetic/queue updates are contract work.
rows.risk: Preserve existing ABI, errors, lifetime and synchronization; no source change recommended.

rows.name: KeSetDisableBoostThread

candidates.name: MmLockUnlockBufferPages: touched-PFN scratch cleanup
candidates.avoidable_cost: BeginPinBatch zeroes 2*(NxpHighestPfn+1) bytes under the PFN lock for every nonempty buffer, even one page. At 32768 PFNs this is 65536 bytes, before two translation walks.
candidates.bounded_change: Retain the existing USHORT multiplicity array, initially zero, and require it zero at every API exit. Track the last translated VA reaching RecordPin, including a current RecordPin that increments then rejects. For successful requests within a fixed small page budget (initial tuning example: 64 pages), clear touched PFN slots during the existing apply pass; for small rejected prefixes use a range-checked per-PFN clear helper over that prefix. For larger successful requests or rejected prefixes exceeding the budget, bulk-reset the existing entire array once at exit instead of walking the prefix again. This moves the baseline full clear from entry to exit under the same PFN lock, rather than adding a second bulk clear. No new permanent table/generation array; budget must be validated by measured crossover.
correctness: Keep the PFN lock across both translation/preflight and mutation; all-or-nothing invalid-range handling remains unchanged.
Preserve alias multiplicity, saturated scratch counts, sticky pin overflow, pending returns, persistence, and invalid-PFN behavior.
Clearing duplicate aliases is safe only after all preflight checks finish; include increment-then-reject and late-invalid exits in cleanup.
No unhandled early return may leave scratch nonzero; initialization and full checked-only invariant assertions must stay outside the release hot path.
Choose sparse/bulk fallback by translated VA-prefix length, bounding cleanup even for many aliases of one PFN. Large rejected prefixes must use one bulk reset, with no extra translation walk.
candidates.risk: Medium: stale scratch after any rejection violates the next preflight; prove zero-on-entry/exit in all branches. Sparse rejection adds at most the fixed page-budget of extra translations. Large-prefix bulk fallback retains one baseline-sized clear and avoids the extra cleanup walk, but moving the clear and adding mode branches still require timing; no universal speedup is claimed.
candidates.measurement: Run the actual baseline and candidate kernel implementation through the exported ordinal in the same release compiler/xemu 128-MiB configuration and immutable guest ISO; at least seven paired trials, alternating order; retain all samples, median and variation. Check exact outputs/state and operation counters first; claim timing improvement only beyond observed variation. No measurements were executed in this read-only audit. Use 0/1/2/16/256/4096-page requests; unaligned ends; overflow; invalid first/middle/last page; repeated aliases to one PFN; nested lock/unlock and exact/over-count unlock; sticky overflow and deferred-free unlock. Count batch bytes cleared, translations and PFN-lock duration; expect successful small calls to clear only touched slots (two bytes per clear rather than full RAM-sized scratch); report worst-case rejection overhead too. Compare small sparse and large bulk modes around 32/64/65/128 pages and early/mid/late rejection in a 4096-page request. Large rejected prefixes should perform one full reset and zero cleanup translations; ensure aliased 4096-page prefixes also fall back.
